context:
The pipeline already iterates through every bundle once. After the
per-benchmark artifacts are built, iterate the in-memory accumulators
again to compute ranks: for each cohort, sort by the cohort's primary
metric and assign 1-based ranks. Aggregate across cohorts per engine.

Frontend is a pure table render. No interactivity in the first cut -
clicking a cohort header navigates to the matrix leaderboard for that
cohort.
description:
The 2026-04-15 strategy review observed that BenchBox's multi-benchmark
story is a real differentiator vs ClickBench but the current Home page
does not lean into it. A cross-benchmark meta-leaderboard answers
"which engines consistently do well across benchmarks?" - a question
no single-benchmark site can answer.

Approach: compute per-engine performance *rank* within each
(benchmark, scale, phase) cohort, then surface aggregate rank across
cohorts. Ranks normalize away the incompatible units (power_score vs
geomean_ms) that make direct cross-benchmark comparison impossible.

Visualization: a compact table on the home page with columns per
benchmark cohort and a cell showing the engine's rank (e.g., "1/4")
plus a summary "Average rank: 1.5" column on the right.

Not included: any claim that the meta-leaderboard is an official or
weighted score. It is a transparent rank-aggregation across whatever
cohorts the corpus contains, with all inputs visible and linkable.

anti_patterns.dont: hide the methodology panel behind a 'why' link
anti_patterns.instead: show it inline below the table
filter them out at pipeline time
use simple rank aggregation with all inputs visible
anti_patterns.why: any weighting is indefensible and masks the inputs

anti_patterns.dont: penalize platforms that didn't run a cohort
anti_patterns.instead: show N/A and exclude from that platform's average
anti_patterns.why: missing data is not a loss

preserves.behavior: Home page remains navigable - the meta-leaderboard is additive, not replacing global nav
No invented composite scores - only transparent rank aggregation
Recent Results section remains on the home page in a secondary position

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c 'import json; d = json.load(open("results-explorer/public/data/meta_leaderboard.json")); assert all(len(c["platforms"]) >= 2 for c in d["cohorts"])'
verifications.description: Meta-leaderboard only includes cohorts with ≥2 platforms

work_units.notes:
